text: . In badminton, Indian shuttlers Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth and Rakshitha Ramraj will play their respective quarterfinal matches at the Hong Kong Open Super 500 tournament today. In men’s singles, Lakshya Sen entered the quarterfinals after defeating Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke 21-11, 21-18. He will next face Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew, while Kidambi Srikanth will take on Thailand’s Kunlavut Vitidsarn this morning.In women’s singles, Rakshitha Ramraj advanced to the quarterfinals after stunning China’s Tokyo Olympic champion Chen Yu Fei 21-18, 24-22. She will next meet Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong. In men’s doubles, the Indian pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty also reached the quarterfinals with a straight-game victory over Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong, 21-19, 21-16. Indian duo will next face China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi today to secure a place in the semifinals.

. Major Asian stock market indices ended on a mixed note today. Taiwan’s Taiex shed 4.4 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped nearly two per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite dipped 0.3 per cent. Conversely, South Korea’s Kospi rose 1.4 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.7 per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times added half a per cent.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 dipped 0.4 per cent while, Germany’s DAX rose 0.2 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Bulgaria Velislava Petrova has arrived in New Delhi for the official visit. She is scheduled to have a meeting with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal in the National Capital today. Later on the day, the Bulgarian Foreign Affairs Minister will also call on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan.She will also have a meeting with External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar in New Delhi tomorrow. Ministry of External Affairs Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the longstanding and friendly relations between India and Bulgaria. He added that the visit will also deepen bilateral cooperation across diverse sectors between the two countries.

. The Reserve Bank has asked banks to focus on building strategy and overcoming risks, especially technology risks. Speaking at an event organised by Excellence Enablers in Mumbai this morning, RBI Deputy Governor S C Murmu said banks need to invest in technology as well as people to ensure there is no wrongdoing.Emphasizing that banks need to mull over whether they will incentivise volumes or customer outcomes, Mr. Murmu said mis-selling rarely begins at the branch counter; pointing out that it begins with a sales target and a variable pay scale. Clarifying that outsourcing an activity does not mean outsourcing responsibility as the onus for outcomes remains with the banks, Mr. Murmu said banks must rethink their reliance on external vendors for certain tasks.Terming the upcoming transition to Expected Credit Loss – ECL framework as a significant milestone, Mr. Murmu said banks will have to provide for losses they expect and not just for losses already incurred. Stating that the system will be shifting to principles based approach, the RBI Deputy Governor said the remaining Basel-III standards will also take effect.With artificial intelligence-based models now driving parts of credit, collections and fraud detection systems, Mr. Murmu underlined that bank boards need to ensure that decisioning is explainable, fair and accountable. He also said that risks from climate change or cyberattacks may not have an immediate impact, but the dent will show up in the loan book sooner or later.

. Ace Indian shuttlers, Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth advanced to the Men’s Singles second round of Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships today. In the opening round, Srikanth defeated Japan’s Koki Watanabe 21-16, 16-21, 21-9 while Lakshya beat France’s Arnaud Merklé 14-21, 21-16, 25-23.In Women’s Singles, Rakshitha Ramraj and Ashmita Chaliha also advanced to the second round. Rakshitha defeated Mia Blichfeldt 21-18, 21-18 while Ashmita defeated compatriot Isharani Baruah 12-21, 21-13, 21-12 in the round of 32.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. President Droupadi Murmu has said that over the past decade, the Government has undertaken several far-reaching initiatives in healthcare and medical education, leading to a significant expansion of healthcare services across all levels, from primary to tertiary care.Addressing the convocation of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in New Delhi today, the President said that currently around one lakh 75 thousand Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are operational across the country, effectively delivering primary healthcare services to people in rural and remote areas.She said, under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana, significant strides have been made in strengthening tertiary healthcare and enhancing the quality of medical education. President Murmu said advanced healthcare facilities, which were once largely concentrated in metropolitan cities, are now reaching Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities as well. She said these initiatives are making primary healthcare more accessible in villages, hospital treatment more affordable for economically weaker sections, emergency medical services available at the district level and super-speciality healthcare facilities accessible across regions.The President said, recognising the evolving healthcare needs of the country, the Central Government introduced the National Health Policy in 2017, with a comprehensive approach that focuses not only on strengthening medical infrastructure but also on promoting preventive and promotive healthcare, ensuring access to medicines, and expanding rehabilitation and palliative care services. She said, in view of the rising of non-communicable diseases, such as diabetes and cancer, along with mental health concerns, focused efforts are being undertaken through various initiatives to strengthen their prevention, early detection and effective management.Highlighting the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, President Murmu said, today access to quality healthcare in India is no longer a privilege reserved exclusively for a select few. She said, these schemes are making a significant contribution, particularly in protecting low-income families from catastrophic healthcare expenditure.In his address, Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda lauded the institute for offering high-quality healthcare services and also for achieving remarkable milestones in research, organ donation and retrieval and various other surgical procedures. The Minister informed that a state-of-the-art super-speciality block is also nearing completion and will become operational very soon. Mr Nadda said, primary education and secondary education and school education are birthrights. However, professional education is not a birthright it is a privilege.He said, professional education and high-quality training that the students are receiving at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences should be recognised as a privilege. He said, in a way, it is society’s contribution to them. Mr Nadda informed that just recently, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approximately 15 thousand crore rupees has been released for around 10 thousand additional undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats. He said, it shows how much priority the Narendra Modi-led government is giving to medical education.The Minister said, the opportunities and resources available to the students are truly a treasure and it is their responsibility to give back this treasure to society through dedicated service and commitment. Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava, Chairman of the National Medical Commission Dr Abhijat Chandrakant Sheth and Director of the Institute Dr. Akhilandeswari Prasad were present on the occasion.

. Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran today said that foreign capital is returning sharply to India as oil prices cool below 100 dollars per barrel and the emerging risks regarding AI valuation. Addressing the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE) in Mumbai, Dr. Nageswaran said India has recorded foreign portfolio inflows of 11.3 billion dollars in just the first 18 days of November.The CEA further underlined that India remains poised to be a big beneficiary in the course of the next financial year as the AI bubble comes down to realistic levels, adding that earlier currency pressures from AI outflows will now likely turn into a source of currency strength. He also highlighted that India has sustained roughly 7 per cent real GDP growth despite global tariff turmoil, supply shocks, and geopolitical conflicts, adding that India has been successful in lifting roughly 500 million people above the 4.20 dollar-a-day moderate poverty line, with rural poverty falling faster than urban in the past decade.While noting that the Indian Government, which had been cautious about trade liberalisation until around 2020, Dr. Nageswaran said that the government has embraced free trade agreements with considerable enthusiasm in the post-pandemic period. He said that India has not only concluded but also operationalised trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand this year alone. He added that a trade agreement with the European Union has also been concluded while trade agreements with the US and Canada are also imminent.Pointing towards India’s strong export performance in the current financial year, the CEA said exports of  goods and services stood at around 569 billion dollars from April to October, registering a growth of nearly 17 percent.Talking about the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the CEA flagged five unique challenges – geopolitical fragmentation, China’s manufacturing scale, the energy trilemma, AI-led job shifts, and social media’s impact on youth cognitive skills. To counter these, the CEA said closing technology gaps will buy resilience for India, while agriculture, trade skills, and human-centric services will buy leverage for India.

. In a significant milestone for India’s presence in overseas education, the first batch of students from IIT Delhi’s Abu Dhabi Campus have graduated. Education Minister Pralhad Joshi presided over the convocation ceremony held today in Abu Dhabi for the inaugural cohort of 17 Students who completed an M. Tech. in Energy Transition and Sustainability. The ceremony was also attended by Shri. Harish Salve (Chairperson, Board of Governors, IIT Delhi), Prof Rangan Banerjee (Director, IIT Delhi) and Prof Shantanu Roy (Executive Director, IIT Delhi – Abu Dhabi). Ms. Rima Al Mokarrab (Executive Director, Strategic Affairs, Executive Affairs Authority of the UAE) and India’s Ambassador to the UAE Dr. Deepak Mittal were also present for the ceremony, apart from other officials and academics from India and the UAE.M. Tech in Energy Transition and Sustainability was the first course to begin at IITD Abu Dhabi in January 2024. During their course, the first batch produced theses spanning areas such as carbon capture, green hydrogen, renewables, energy markets and methane – addressing various challenges rooted in the energy sector. Notably, a student – Adnan Aboud Hajsalem Saleh Nagah, scored a perfect 10 GPA in the batch and was awarded Gold Medal for his academic excellence.The decision to establish an IIT in UAE goes back to February 2022, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the then Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan agreed to establish an Indian Institute of Technology in the United Arab Emirates during their Virtual Summit. In July 2023, an MoU was signed between the Ministry of Education of India, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT Delhi) and Abu Dhabi Department of Education & Knowledge (ADEK) during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to UAE in July 2023 – to establish IIT Delhi – Abu Dhabi.The IITD – Abu Dhabi campus today offers 6 programmes and includes students and research scholars from across 13 nationalities. Apart from the M. Tech course, the Institute also offers a Ph.D. program in Energy and Sustainability, establishing an early focus on advanced research and innovation in critical sustainability domains. The undergraduate (UG) programs currently include Chemical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Energy Engineering, and Electrical Engineering.

Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi today. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day forum aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of the region, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation.The inaugural ceremony will feature Civilisations in Conversation – Cultural Show, a presentation combining music, dance, visual storytelling and narration. The Forum will also feature exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage titled ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence. It will offer an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE.Four thematic sessions will be held on 21st and 22nd November, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives. Discussions will cover cultural expressions such as music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine and traditional games.

. Russian President Vladimir Putin today vowed to retaliate after Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge linking Russia and Crimea. Mr. Putin told media person in Shenzhen that Russia will respond to these attacks.The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside European leaders.A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia and  Crimea halted rail traffic. Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage.

. In Men’s Cricket, an unbeaten 173-run stand between Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips took host New Zealand to 243 at the loss of 5 wickets at stumps on Day 1 of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington today.Nicholls, who slammed his 12th Test century, finished unbeaten on 113, while Phillips will resume his innings on 94 on Day 2. For India, Jasprit Bumrah scalped 3 wickets, while Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep took one wicket each.Earlier, India won the toss and opted to bowl.

. The Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ which crossed the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coast earlier today, has moved north-northeastwards and weakened into a Deep Depression. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that the Deep depression is likely to move north-northeastwards and gradually weaken into a Depression in the next six hours and a Well-marked Low-Pressure area in the subsequent six hours.The Met Department has advised the fishermen not to venture into West Central and Northwest Bay of Bengal till tomorrow morning. The Weather Agency has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Odisha for the day. It has also issued an orange colour warning for heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal and Jharkhand for the day.

. Young batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi,, women’s World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet Kaur, Olympic medallists Lovlina Borgohain and Mirabai Chanu were among nine Indian sporting stars named in the TIME100 Next India list.World champion chess player D Gukesh, women’s 400 meter hurdles national record holder Vithya Ramraj, Asian Games gold-winning archer Kumkum Mohod, women’s hockey team goalkeeper Savita Punia and former tennis star Sania Mirza also figured in the prestigious list.TIME has brought out the list for the first time in India. Sooryavanshi, Chanu and Kumkum were listed in the ‘Innovators’ section, while Borgohain, Gukesh and Vithya were named among the Phenoms. Savita figured among the Leaders, while Sania and Harmanpreet found places among the Advocates.

. In badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty stormed into the quarterfinals of the Hong Kong Open Super 500 badminton tournament today. The Indian duo defeated Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong with a straight-game win 21-19, 21-16. Satwik and Chirag will next face China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi, who beat Japan’s Kakeru Kumagai and Hiroki Nishi 21-19, 21-17.On the other hand, India’s Lakshya Sen will take on Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in the men’s singles pre-quarterfinals later in the day.In the women’s doubles, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, the bronze medallist at the World Championships in New Delhi, lost to the American pair of Lauren Lam and Allison Lee 20-22, 13-21 in the pre-quarterfinals to end their campaign

. The Indian men’s hockey team began its campaign at the 2026 India-New Zealand Century of Sporting Unity Event with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over the hosts in Auckland, New Zealand today.At the Lloyd Elsmore Hockey Stadium, New Zealand took the lead in the 25th minute through Jonty Elmes, who converted a penalty corner into goal. India responded immediately with Uttam Singh finding the equaliser with a field goal.India stepped up their attacking efforts in the second half, with Shardanand Tiwari scoring a field goal to put the visitors ahead. Captain Sanjay then extended country’s advantage with a penalty-corner conversion, taking the score to 3-1. New Zealand continued to push for a goal and reduced the deficit through Sam Hiha, who scored a field goal.India held on to their advantage in the closing stages to secure a 3-2 win and begin the three-match series on a positive note. India will next face New Zealand on Saturday, followed by the third match on Sunday.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India and the United States are natural partners in building trusted and resilient supply chains amid global uncertainty. He said this while speaking at the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit organised by the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce in New Delhi.He emphasised the significance of the India-US economic partnership, noting that the United States contributes capital, technology, and innovation, while India provides scale, talent, manufacturing strength, and competitiveness. The Minister underscored that trust forms the foundation of India’s international partnerships, affirming that India offers a trusted partnership and stands by its friends through difficult times.Referring to his recent visit to Italy, Mr Goyal asserted that India and Italy have the potential to expand trade to 50 billion euros following the implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement. He stated that the benefits of global trade, international engagement, and preferential, free trade, and bilateral trade agreements must reach the smallest businesses and individuals. He added that these benefits should extend to MSMEs, farmers, fishermen, Vishwakarmas, artisans, and handicraft and handloom makers.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. Prime Minister of Nepal Balendra Shah will pay a two-day State visit to India starting Sunday(Nov 22). This will be his first visit to India after assuming office in March this year. During the visit, the Prime Minister of Nepal will call on President Droupadi Murmu.Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold bilateral talks with his Nepalese counterpart on Monday(Nov 23) to review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. Ministry of External Affairs said India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties.Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports.The Ministry said the visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal under its ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. It will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the bilateral partnership and advance mutually beneficial cooperation.

. Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. In Football, India clinched a record-extending 10th SAFF Championship title, beating arch-rivals Pakistan 2-1 in a thrilling final to retain their crown at the National Stadium in Dhaka last night.The Blue Tigers also made history by winning the tournament for the third consecutive time. For India, Suhail Ahmad Bhat in 60th and Sandip Mandi in 88th minute scored goals. India had booked their place in the final after defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the semi-final on Saturday.Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated the Indian men’s football team for winning a historic hat-trick of SAFF Championship titles in Dhaka. Congratulating the team on social media, Dr. Mandaviya hailed the achievement and praised the players for completing a hat-trick of consecutive titles.

. The Indian women’s hockey team defeated Malaysia 4-1 in the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy being held in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Khan Mumtaz, captain Salima Tete, Pooja Sahu and Lalremsiami scored one goal each for India. Nuramirah Zulkifli scored the only goal for Malaysia.Earlier in the day, China defeated Thailand 7-0 in the opening match. Feng Qiagmiao and Deng Qiuchan scored two goals each for China, while three other players scored one goal each.In the second match of the day, Japan defeated South Korea 1-0. The match remained goalless until the final minutes. In the 59th minute, Saito Hanami scored from a penalty corner to give Japan the win.Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav inaugurated the tournament today. The stadium was lit up with a grand fireworks display, and a large number of spectators came to watch the matches. Six countries, including India, are taking part in the tournament.The tournament is being held at the International Sports Complex in Barkheda Nathu, Bhopal, from November 19 to 28. Entry to the stadium is free for spectators.On Saturday, China will play Malaysia at 2:30 PM, Thailand will face Japan at 4:45 PM, and hosts India will take on South Korea at 7 PM.

. The Supreme Court today dismissed the two applications filed by the State of Tamil Nadu seeking directions to the State of Karnataka to release 11 TMC of water in the Cauvery River. A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Singh passed the order. Tamil Nadu had moved the Supreme Court seeking implementation of the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s directions requiring Karnataka to release water to the State, amid allegations that it was not receiving its stipulated share of the river water. However, the Karnataka government denied the allegations, stating that it was complying with the orders of the Cauvery Water Management Authority.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will be inaugurated this evening in Goa with a grand ceremony at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium in Taleigao. The nine-day festival will bring together filmmakers, artists and cinema enthusiasts from across the world, celebrating the diversity of Indian and international cinema.It will showcase a wide range of films competing for the prestigious Golden Peacock and Silver Peacock Awards. Addressing the media, Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker highlighted the significance of this year’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’. He emphasised the importance of storytelling that transcends geographical, linguistic and cultural boundaries. Meanwhile, the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar was inaugurated today in Goa as part of IFFI 2026. Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the five-day marketplace is being held at Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon.It brings together filmmakers, producers, writers, investors, distributors and other industry professionals to explore collaborations and connect Indian cinema with global markets. Speaking at the inauguration, IFFI Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker highlighted the power of cinema to enable people to see things differently. He noted that the marketplace engages with filmmakers at every stage of their creative journey, from unfinished scripts to completed films seeking an audience. He encouraged delegates to make the most of the platform, interact with one another and turn conversations into meaningful collaborations.Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, also highlighted the role of WAVES Film Bazaar in bridging the gap between creative ideas and commercial opportunities by connecting filmmakers with investors, distributors and international partners. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call to ‘Create in India, Create for the World’, he emphasised the need to provide Indian creative talent with greater access to international markets. He also highlighted the growth of Film Bazaar from 204 delegates representing 18 countries in 2007 to more than 2,500 delegates in recent editions.Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat, and NFDC Chairman G. Krishnakumar were also present on the occasion. This year’s IFFI features several new attractions under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’. Akashvani correspondents reported that the stage is set, the red carpet is ready, and Goa is all geared up to welcome the world of cinema. Two new sections, ‘Films About Films’ and a dedicated Animation segment, have been introduced this year. While the former will showcase five international productions exploring the lives and creative journeys of filmmakers and the art of cinema, the Animation section will feature five acclaimed films from Japan, France, China, Singapore and the United States.The festival also places a special focus on BRICS cinema, with India’s Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (Part 1) selected as the opening film of the BRICS showcase. Spain has been named the Country of Honour, while Russia is the Partner Country. The international line-up features more than 150 films from 86 countries, alongside 76 films in 18 languages under the Indian Panorama section. Adding to the inaugural celebrations, three-time Grammy Award-winning composer Ricky Kej will lead a special symphonic orchestra presentation, blending cinema, music and cultural performances.

. Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan has highlighted the importance of healthy livestock in the prosperity of farmers in the country. In an article for a daily newspaper, Mr Chouhan said that keeping animals and birds safe from infectious diseases is not just a veterinary issue but a responsibility to protect the livelihood of farmers and the national economy.He said that animal husbandry, dairy and poultry play a vital role in the agricultural economy; hence, prevention of animal diseases and availability of effective vaccines are integral to the country’s agricultural development strategy. The Minister highlighted that India has made significant progress in indigenous vaccine development against animal and poultry diseases over the past decade. Mr Chouhan emphasised that Indian scientists are now capable of developing innovative solutions to animal diseases according to the needs of the country.The Minister further said that India’s goal is not only to protect its livestock and poultry but also to become a leading global supplier of affordable, effective and quality animal vaccines. Mr Chouhan added that healthy livestock, a secure poultry sector and prosperous farmers are important pillars in India’s journey of Viksit Bharat.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. The Government has approved the establishment of a Medical College at the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research of Chandigarh’s Sarangpur campus. In a social media post, Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda said that this project will be developed at an investment of 456 crore rupees and will have an annual intake of 125 MBBS students.Spread across nearly 51 acres, the college will feature modern laboratories, advanced simulation facilities, clinical training and research infrastructure, nurturing the next generation of skilled medical professionals. Mr Nadda added that the approval marks another significant step towards fulfilling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of adding 75 thousand medical seats in the country over the next five years. He said that the initiative will strengthen medical education and help develop a skilled healthcare workforce in the country.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for a drone attack on a tower in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, causing material damage but no casualties. Saudi Arabia’s Directorate General of Civil Defence said the attack damaged a building in the King Abdullah Financial District. Media reports said the strike shattered windows across seven to eight floors of the Public Investment Fund Tower and damaged parts of its exterior facade.The tower houses the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed several Houthi drones in the southern region of the country. Civil Defence also issued danger alerts for several areas, including Najran, Riyadh, Al Kharj, Jizan, Abha and Khamis Mushait. Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported that the group claimed four military operations targeting strategic sites in Saudi Arabia.Its spokesperson said the first operation targeted Riyadh’s financial district early Thursday, followed by another strike in the evening. The Houthis claimed that the attacks scored direct hits and caused significant damage.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has urged Indian businesses to utilise opportunities opened by recent free trade agreements(FTAs). Addressing the valedictory session of FICCI’s Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said, India’s preferential access to global markets has expanded by an additional 60 trillion dollars over the last four-and-a-half years, taking the total to approximately 70 trillion dollars.Referring to his recent visits to Egypt and Italy, the Minister said that the growing interest of international partners in working with India reflects the country’s increasing global standing. He noted that discussions have been initiated to explore a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement with Egypt, while the forthcoming India-EU FTA has generated considerable interest among Italian businesses. He said that the commitment of international businesses to work with India reflects the growing opportunities for trade, investment and industrial cooperation.Highlighting the country’s growing economic strength and global engagement, Mr Goyal said that India has set a target of achieving 1 trillion dollars in exports in Financial Year 2026-27. He noted that the country recorded exports of 480 billion dollars in the first six months of the current financial year. The Minister spoke about India’s transformation over the past decade, noting improvements in infrastructure, digital connectivity, financial inclusion and the banking sector. He added that the country’s growing middle class, purchasing power and expanding domestic market provide a strong foundation for economic growth.

. In Men’s Cricket, Impressive fifties from openers Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul helped India reach 159 for one in their first innings at stumps in reply to New Zealand’s first-innings total of 368 in the first Test of the two-match series in Wellington. At stumps, Devdutt Padikkal (16 batting) was giving company to Rahul with India trailing by 209 runs.Earlier, India won the toss and elected to bowl; Jasprit Bumrah and the Indian seamers reduced the hosts to 70/5 before a massive sixth-wicket recovery shifted the momentum. Henry Nicholls anchors the innings unbeaten on 140 runs in 282 balls, having shared a 200-plus stand with Glenn Phillips, who was dismissed for 118 runs in 216 balls.This series marks the final leg of India’s tour of New Zealand, with valuable ICC World Test Championship points on the line. Steered by Shubman Gill, the 16-member squad features KL Rahul as vice-captain, alongside key players like Rishabh Pant, Jasprit Bumrah, and Ravindra Jadeja.

. In Bangladesh, industrial unrest disrupted production at 61 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia, near Dhaka, amid workers’ demands for a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka. Clashes between workers and police in Ashulia left three policemen injured. Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters. In a separate incident in Savar, a 40-year-old man was detained after allegedly throwing a crude bomb from a footbridge.In Sylhet, four parked buses were set on fire in the Chalibandar area. Firefighters brought the blaze under control. Authorities are investigating the incidents, while tension continues in several areas.Meanwhile, fresh incidents of violence and arson were reported in several parts of the country today, as activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations enforced a nationwide lockdown programme.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 16 paise to close at 93 rupees and 29 paise against the US dollar. The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.69 in intra-day trade.

. Union Minister of Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution & New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi is on an official visit to the UAE.In Dubai, Mr Joshi held bilateral discussions with Omar Sultan Al Olama, UAE’s Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications. Discussions focused on AI-enabled learning, digital public infrastructure for education, STEM education, teacher capacity building and the responsible use of emerging technologies in classrooms. The two Ministers also explored the potential of the IIT Delhi-Abu Dhabi campus as a bridge for joint AI research with Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, along with research collaboration under SPARC (Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration) in areas such as AI, climate resilience, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing and space technologies. They also exchanged perspectives on the UAE’s National AI Literacy Curriculum Framework (K-12) and National AI Upskilling Programme for Teachers and a proposal for a structured India-UAE dialogue on AI in education.Earlier Mr Joshi presided over the convocation ceremony of the first batch of graduates from IIT Delhi’s Abu Dhabi Campus. Addressing the convocation ceremony, he highlighted the rapid growth of India-UAE cooperation in higher education, describing the campus as a strong example of the partnership between the two countries. He noted that the campus, which had a modest beginning in January 2024, has expanded its academic programmes and research infrastructure in less than three years. He also highlighted India’s growing global academic presence, underlining the strong showing of Indian Universities in the QS rankings.Crediting the National Education Policy 2020 under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, the Minister said India’s education system was moving beyond rote learning towards critical thinking, research and innovation. He also pointed to the growing internationalisation of higher education, with Indian institutions expanding overseas and foreign universities establishing campuses in India. Calling the graduates a generation of bridge-builders, the Minister said their understanding of both Indian and UAE markets would create significant opportunities, particularly as bilateral trade and economic cooperation continue to expand.

. In Badminton, the Indian Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty advanced to the second round of Hong Kong Super 500 tournament today. The star Indian pair defeated Chinese Taipei’s Lee Jhe-huei and Yang Po-han, 15-21, 21-17, 28-26 in their opening round match.Earlier in the day, Indian mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Radhika Sharma progressed to the main draw of the tounramnet with a straight-game win. They took just 36 minutes to beat Hong Kong’s Cheng Ying Kit and Leung Yuet Yee, 21-17 21-17.Indian Shuttlers Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth will begin their campaign in Men’s Singles tomorrow.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has highlighted the strong complementarities between Indian innovation and Italian enterprise, stressing the vast potential for collaboration in sectors such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and automobiles. Addressing the plenary session of the Fourth India-Italy Business and Innovation Forum in Rome, alongside Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, Goyal urged businesses from both countries to look beyond traditional trade and explore new avenues of economic and technological cooperation. He also highlighted India’s development achievements, noting that 496 million people had been lifted out of extreme poverty in just 12 years.Interacting with startups at the India-Italy Innovation Forum, he said he had heard from entrepreneurs on both sides about how they developed their ideas and built businesses around them. He encouraged Indian and Italian startups to explore partnerships in each other’s markets to expand their reach and accelerate growth. Emphasising the importance of such platforms for young entrepreneurs, Goyal said opportunities like these could open doors to major business breakthroughs.Reaffirming the commitment to strengthen bilateral economic ties, Goyal said that with expanding opportunities for businesses, startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), both countries are working towards achieving their bilateral trade target of 20 billion euros by 2029. He expressed confidence that the growing economic engagement would take the India-Italy partnership to the next level.

. Amnesty International has urged Bangladesh authorities to stop arresting and harassing garment workers and trade union leaders demanding higher minimum wages. The human rights organisation has expressed concern over what it described as a crackdown on labour activists.Amnesty has called on the government to respect the right to peaceful assembly and distinguish peaceful protesters from those involved in violence. The appeal follows the detention of Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation President Sultana Begum and General Secretary Md Elias by Detective Branch police on November 17. They were detained after participating in a webinar on minimum-wage protests. They reportedly face allegations of obstructing police duties and vandalising factories.Five other labour activists and union representatives were also arrested earlier this month. They include Mostafa Kamal, Rozina Akter Sumi, Md Ali Azgar, Md Morshed Alam Kawsar and Md Fuadur Rahman Nirjon. Amnesty International has called for an end to the targeting of workers exercising their labour rights.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for greater Jan Bhagidari or community participation, in the early identification of disabilities and overcoming social stigma. Addressing the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment in New Delhi, Mr Modi said that community participation can play a significant role in creating awareness among parents about developmental disabilities and the importance of early identification.He emphasised that the spirit of competitive and cooperative federalism should guide implementation, with states learning from one another’s experiences and innovations. Mr Modi also advised that states could organise start-up competitions to encourage young innovators to develop affordable aids and assistive devices.Highlighting the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan – Drug-Free India Campaign, Prime Minister stressed that efforts to address substance abuse must go beyond routine and symbolic activities. He suggested involving schools through essay-writing, debates, oratory competitions, and other activities to generate awareness among young people and encourage wider societal participation.

. Global crude oil prices were trading with gains today. Brent crude was trading 0.7 per cent up at 92 US dollars and 61 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.4 per cent up at 83 US dollars and 60 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the sixth Pre-Budget Consultation with the experts and stakeholders from the Information Technology sector in connection with the forthcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur, CEO of NITI Aayog, Anurag Jain and Chief Economic Adviser Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran. Senior officials from Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology also attended the meeting.Later on the day, the Finance Minister chaired the seventh Pre-Budget Consultation with the experts from the infrastructure, energy, and sustainability sectors in connection with the forthcoming Union Budget. The meeting was attended by Secretaries of the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, and the CEA. Senior officials from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways also attended the meeting.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. Presidents of the US, China and Russia concluded their unprecedented trilateral meeting yesterday by issuing a Declaration Towards Peace, calling for UN reforms and outlining plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products to ease the energy crisis. The three Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin – in their four-point declaration also agreed to hold dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.They also agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for the three-way summit on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen. Trump had expressed his intention to discuss nuclear arms reductions and other major international issues at the three-way summit.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Clashes broke out between activists of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the banned Awami League in Bera upazila of Pabna district in Bangladesh. According to local media reports, tensions escalated after Awami League supporters took out a sudden protest procession and marched towards Bera Model Police Station, raising slogans.BNP and its student wing, Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, activists reached the spot and chased the protesters, triggering clashes and counter-chases. The procession was later dispersed. Later, a haystack near the abandoned residence of former Deputy Speaker Shamsul Haque Tuku was set on fire, and the house was reportedly vandalised. Police confirmed the fire but said the identities of those involved in the arson and vandalism were yet to be established.

. Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal has condemned repeated attacks on commercial vessels, particularly those involving Indian seafarers. He made these remarks in New Delhi during a review of the situation aimed at strengthening maritime safety and security measures, as the ministry tracks nine India-flagged or Indian-interest vessels west of the Strait of Hormuz.He asserted that such incidents pose a serious threat to the safety and security of seafarers, disrupt maritime trade and undermine the stability of global supply chains. The Union Minister emphasised that freedom of navigation and the unimpeded movement of merchant vessels through international waters are fundamental principles of international maritime law.He also stressed that ensuring safe and secure sea lanes is essential not only for the continuity of global trade but also for sustaining economic growth, energy security and the prosperity of nations. Mr Sonowal has directed the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) and all concerned officers to further strengthen maritime safety and security measures. The Union Minister has also reviewed the victims’ compensation status and directed the Director General of Shipping to personally brief him on the progress.He also enquired about measures to ensure timely assistance to the victims’ next of kin. The ministry’s E-Navik seafarer tracking module is tracking more than 800 vessels in the Persian Gulf, west of the Strait of Hormuz, and more than 200 vessels in the Gulf of Oman, east of the Strait of Hormuz.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold dropped over 1.2 per cent to 1,29,531 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also declined two per cent to 1,60,439 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. IIT Madras has invited registrations for the January 2027 batch of its School Connect Programme, aimed at introducing school students to emerging technologies and new career opportunities. The eight-week online certificate courses will begin on 11th January 2027. Students of Classes 9 to 12 can enrol in 20 courses covering subjects such as Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Aerospace Engineering and Cybersecurity.The programme has so far enrolled over two lakh 25 thousand students from more than 6,500 partner schools across the country. The registration deadline is 8th January 2027, and the course fee is 500 rupees per course. Interested students can register through the IIT Madras School Connect website. The initiative is implemented by the Centre for Outreach and Digital Education at IIT Madras.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.
